propositions: Handing a failed verifier attempt's search frontier as an exclusion list (zero imperative sentences, data-shaped evidence block) to resume arms does not reduce re-search overlap by the predeclared 30% threshold on both corpus tickets.
Treatment arm (B) with frontier block showed +78% relative increase in overlap rate on ticket 45c1 and +60% increase on ticket 8d74 versus control arm (A), both failing the GO criterion.

The fence rendering the frontier block inert by design allowed the model to immediately re-execute tool calls explicitly listed under 'searched-and-empty', raising measured overlap rather than reducing it.

Argument-level tool-call transcripts (paths, patterns, result classifications) must be captured per verifier run to measure re-search overlap, but production telemetry today carries only aggregate request counts and the verdict cache deliberately stores no tool arguments.

Cache-seeded resumption already removes the dominant redundancy (re-proving credited criteria); remaining re-grounding of unproven criteria cannot be suppressed by an untrusted data-shaped exclusion list inside a fenced context.
